data.title: Spanish or Italian?
data.statement:
Spanish and Italian are both Romance languages, descended from Latin. They both use the Latin alphabet, but in slightly different ways. 

For example, while both use acute accents (´) over some vowels, only Italian uses grave (`) and circumflex (^) accents. Also, while both use exclamation points (!) and question marks (?), only Spanish uses their inverted versions (¡ and ¿), which always appear in the same sentence as their right-side up counterparts. Finally, Spanish has a unique letter (ñ) that does not appear in Italian.

Given an input string, determine which language the phrase is written in, Spanish or Italian, or if there isn't enough information to know.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Spanish and Italian are both Romance languages, descended from Latin. They both use the Latin alphabet, but in slightly different ways.

For example, while both use acute accents (´) over some vowels, only Italian uses grave (`) and circumflex (^) accents. Also, while both use exclamation points (!) and question marks (?), only Spanish uses their inverted versions (¡ and ¿), which always appear in the same sentence as their right-side up counterparts. Finally, Spanish has a unique letter (ñ) that does not appear in Italian.

Given an input string, determine which language the phrase is written in, Spanish or Italian, or if there isn't enough information to know.
Input
One line that contains a phrase as a string, written in either Spanish or Italian, p.
Output
A string that contains the language the phrase is written in, either Spanish or Italian. If there isn’t enough information to know which it is, output Unclear.
Constraints
Inputs will have full sentences.
Example
Input
¿Cómo estás?
Output
Spanish
